arxiv-2105-03468.title: zeus : A Python implementation of Ensemble Slice Sampling for efficient Bayesian parameter inference 2021 zeus : A Python implementation of Ensemble Slice Sampling for efficient Bayesian parameter inference – A
arxiv-2105-03468.creator: Minas Karamanis, Florian Beutler, John A. Peacock
arxiv-2105-03468.description: Abstract We introduce zeus , a well-tested Python implementation of the Ensemble Slice Sampling (ESS) method for Bayesian parameter inference. ESS is a novel Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm specifically designed to tackle the computational challenges posed by modern astronomical and cosmological analyses.

arxiv-2106-00141.title: Proactive Provenance Policies for Automatic Cryptographic Data Centric Security
arxiv-2106-00141.creator: Shamaria Engram, Tyler Kaczmarek, Alice Lee, David Bigelow
arxiv-2106-00141.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shamaria Engram, Tyler Kaczmarek, Alice Lee, David Bigelow. Data provenance analysis has been used as an assistive measure for ensuring system integrity. However, such techniques are typically reactive approaches to identify the root cause of an attack in its aftermath. This is in part due to fact that the collection of provenance metadata often results in a deluge of information that cannot easily be queried and analyzed in real time.

arxiv-2203-12423.title: Polarization-resolving graphene-based mid-infrared detector
arxiv-2203-12423.creator: Valentin Semkin, Dmitry Mylnikov, Elena Titova, Sergey Zhukov, Dmitry Svintsov
arxiv-2203-12423.description: Abstract The ability to resolve the polarization of light with on-chip devices represents an urgent problem in optoelectronics. The detectors with polarization resolution demonstrated so far mostly require multiple oriented detectors or movable external polarizers. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the feasibility to resolve the polarization of mid-infrared light with a single chemical-vapor-deposited graphene-channel device with dissimilar metal contacts.

arxiv-2205-02055.title: Planning a Cost-Effective Delay-Constrained Passive Optical Network for 5G Fronthaul Abdulhalim Fayad, Manish Jha, and Tibor Cinkler are with Department of Telecommunications and Media Informatics, Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary. Jacek Rak and Tibor Cinkler are with Departm
arxiv-2205-02055.creator: Abdulhalim Fayad, Manish Jha, Tibor Cinkler, and Jacek Rak
arxiv-2205-02055.description: Abstract With the rapid growth in the telecommunications industry moving towards 5G and beyond (5GB) and the emergence of data-hungry and time-sensitive applications, Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) are faced with a considerable challenge to keep up with these new demands. Cloud radio access network (CRAN) has emerged as a cost-effective architecture that improves 5GB performance.

arxiv-2302-13576.title: X-ray spectral correlations in a sample of Low-mass black hole X-ray binaries in the hard state
arxiv-2302-13576.creator: Bei You, Yanting Dong, Zhen Yan, Zhu Liu, Youli Tuo, Yuanle Yao, Xinwu Cao
arxiv-2302-13576.description: Abstract The power-law emission and reflection component provide valuable insights into the accretion process around a black hole. In this work, thanks to the broadband spectra coverage of the Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope Array , we study the spectral properties for a sample of low-mass black hole X-ray binaries (BHXRBs).

arxiv-2309-09086.title: Split Federated Learning for 6G Enabled-Networks: Requirements, Challenges and Future Directions
arxiv-2309-09086.creator: Houda Hafi, Bouziane Brik, Pantelis A. Frangoudis, and Adlen Ksentini
arxiv-2309-09086.description: Abstract Sixth-generation (6G) networks anticipate intelligently supporting a wide range of smart services and innovative applications. Such a context urges a heavy usage of Machine Learning (ML) techniques, particularly Deep Learning (DL), to foster innovation and ease the deployment of intelligent network functions/operations, which are able to fulfill the various requirements of the envisioned 6G services.

arxiv-2312-14941.title: Multi-Criteria Client Selection and Scheduling with Fairness Guarantee for Federated Learning Service
arxiv-2312-14941.creator: Meiying Zhang 1 , Huan Zhao 1 , Sheldon Ebron 1 , Ruitao Xie 2 , Kan Yang 1
arxiv-2312-14941.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) enables multiple clients to train machine learning models collaboratively without sharing the raw training data. However, for a given FL task, how to select a group of appropriate clients fairly becomes a challenging problem due to budget restrictions and client heterogeneity.

arxiv-2403-17941.title: Entanglement of temporal sections as quantum histories and their quantum correlation bounds
arxiv-2403-17941.creator: Marcin Nowakowski
arxiv-2403-17941.description: Abstract In this paper we focus on the underlying quantum structure of temporal correlations and show their peculiar nature which differentiate them from spatial quantum correlations. With a growing interest in representation of quantum states as topological objects, we consider quantum history bundles based on the temporal manifold and show the source of violation of monogamous temporal Bell-like inequalities.

arxiv-2405-13499.title: Euclid : Early Release Observations – Deep anatomy of nearby galaxies Thanks: This paper is published on behalf of the Euclid Consortium.
arxiv-2405-13499.creator: L. K. Hunt, F. Annibali, J.-C. Cuillandre, A. M. N. Ferguson, P. Jablonka, S. S. Larsen, F. R. Marleau, E. Schinnerer, M. Schirmer, C. Stone, C. Tortora, T. Saifollahi, A. arxiv-2405-13499.description: Abstract Euclid is poised to make significant advances in the study of nearby galaxies in the Local Universe. Here we present a first look at six galaxies observed for the Nearby Galaxy Showcase as part of the Euclid Early Release Observations acquired between August and November, 2023.

arxiv-2406-05561.title: Learning Human Detected Differences in Directed Acyclic Graphs
arxiv-2406-05561.creator: Kathrin Guckes (née Ballweg), Alena Beyer, Prof. Margit Pohl, Prof. Tatiana von Landesberger
arxiv-2406-05561.description: Abstract Prior research has shown that human perception of similarity differs from mathematical measures in visual comparison tasks, including those involving directed acyclic graphs. This divergence can lead to missed differences and skepticism about algorithmic results. To address this, we aim to learn the structural differences humans detect in graphs visually.

arxiv-2512-03051.title: Harmonic Extension for Multiscale Analysis and Modeling Near Boundaries, with an Ocean Application
arxiv-2512-03051.description: Abstract Treatment of fields near domain boundaries is a long-standing problem in signal processing that has come into renewed focus following recent efforts in convolution-based multiscale coarse-graining and in machine-learned parameterizations due to ocean boundary artifacts. Here, we propose a general and principled method for extending fields beyond the domain boundaries by solving a Laplace boundary-value problem.

pmc-11301026.title: The role of intraspecific trait variation in driving post‐metamorphic survival: Implications for recruitment in open populations
pmc-11301026.creator: Luis Giménez, Stuart R Jenkins
pmc-11301026.description: Most ecological studies attempting to understand causes of population dynamics and community structure disregard intraspecific trait variation. We quantified the importance of natural intra‐cohort variation in body size and density of juveniles for recruitment of a sessile marine organism, the barnacle Semibalanus balanoides.

pmc-11436735.title: Noninvasive multi-cancer detection using blood-based cell-free microRNAs
pmc-11436735.creator: Jason Zhang, Hallgeir Rui, Hai Hu
pmc-11436735.description: Patients diagnosed with early-stage cancers have a substantially higher chance of survival than those with late-stage diseases. However, the option for early cancer screening is limited, with most cancer types lacking an effective screening tool. Here we report a miRNA-based blood test for multi-cancer early detection based on examination of serum microRNA microarray data from cancer patients and controls.

pmc-11468426.title: A novel drip-irrigative technique for enhanced epiretinal perfluorocarbon liquid clearance during vitreoretinal surgery
pmc-11468426.creator: Jingli Guo, Victoria Y Gu, Yuhan Zhou, Peiquan Zhao, Dongsheng Zhao
pmc-11468426.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeTo present a novel intraoperative application technique of basic salt solution (BSS) perfusate to address residual epiretinal perfluorocarbon liquid (PFCL) droplets.MethodsFollowing standard liquid-gas exchange and aspiration of visible PFCL using a flute needle, the adjuvant drip-irrigative method is employed. A 2mL needle containing BSS is introduced and maneuvered circumferentially around the posterior pole while injecting BSS intermittently to obviate droplet presence.

pmc-11499839.title: Comparing outcomes of patients with early active rheumatoid arthritis initially treated on an inpatient or outpatient basis: a posthoc analysis of the CORRA trial
pmc-11499839.creator: Anna Mai, Dietmar Krause, Renate Klaassen-Mielke, Katharina Meiszl, Nina Timmesfeld, Xenofon Baraliakos, Jürgen Braun
pmc-11499839.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveTreatment strategies of patients with active rheumatoid arthritis (RA) vary within and between countries. While most patients in Germany are treated on an outpatient basis, some are hospitalised (inpatients). In the recently published randomised CORRA (CORRA, CORticoid bridging in Rheumatoid Arthritis) trial, we studied two 12 week glucocorticoid (GC) bridging strategies in patients with early RA comparing high or low GC doses with placebo, followed by an extension phase of 9 months.

pmc-11689065.title: SOFT-TISSUE COMPOSITION ASYMMETRY PREDICTS LEG MUSCLE STRENGTH CHANGES OVER FIVE YEARS AMONG ICELANDIC OLDER ADULTS
pmc-11689065.creator: Milan Chang (Gudjonsson), Marco Recenti, Carlo Ricciardi, Alfonso Maria Ponsiglione, Francesco Amato, Magnus Kjartan Gislason, Paolo Gargiulo
pmc-11689065.description: BackgroundAge-related functional decline emphasizes the need to investigate how tissue composition impacts mobility and independence in older adults. One of the most critical functions associated with mobility disability among older adults is leg muscle strength. The current study investigated the significance of lower leg tissue composition asymmetry on leg muscle strength changes over 5 years among older adults.

pmc-12569960.title: A Hidden Risk of Levodopa: A Case Report of Drug-Induced Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion (SIADH) and Hyponatraemia
pmc-12569960.creator: Salwa Haddy, Pankaj Singh, Elodia Brunetti, Juan Pedro Simon-Turriate
pmc-12569960.description: Hyponatraemia is a common electrolyte imbalance in hospitalised patients, particularly among the elderly. While often mild, asymptomatic, and largely self-resolving, severe cases can lead to significant neurological complications. We report a 67-year-old woman with Parkinson’s disease and chronic hyponatremia who developed acute symptomatic hyponatraemia after starting levodopa/carbidopa. Her sodium levels dropped to 108 mmol/L, with associated confusion.

pmc-13043614.title: Transcortical versus transsylvian approaches for adult insular glioma resection: a systematic review with subanalysis by Berger–Sanai segmentation
pmc-13043614.creator: Gustavo Wagner Baratti Rocha, Paulo Gabriel Sacramento de Silva, Gabriela Monteiro Pereira, Enzo Muzi, Victor de Souza Antunes, Bruno Sodré Serra Antunes, Gabriela Luiza Veloso Maia, Luccas Leite da Silva, Marcos Vinícius Calfat Maldaun, Enrico Ghizoni, Cleiton Formentin
pmc-13043614.description: Insular gliomas pose a neurosurgical challenge due to their deep location and proximity to other structures. The transsylvian (TS) and transcortical (TC) approaches remain the main techniques, guided by the Berger–Sanai (BS) classification. This study compares outcomes across BS zones.

pmc-13118091.title: Presence and Variability of the Microbiome in Perivascular Adipose Tissue: A Whole-Genome Sequencing Study in Dahl SS Rats
pmc-13118091.creator: Sameera Mahimkar, Janice M. Thompson, Christopher B. Blackwood, Stephanie W. Watts, Carolina B. Restini
pmc-13118091.description: Background: Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) contains adipocytes and a stromal-vascular fraction with immune cells that modulate the adjacent vasculature. The presence of immune cells in PVAT of vascular beds is poorly understood—are they resident or recruited? We propose a novel resident microbiome present in PVAT, given the immune-rich stromal environment.

pmc-13205805.title: Model-Based Financial Consequences of Electrical Stimulation Therapy for Pressure Injury Healing
pmc-13205805.creator: Yoshiyuki Yoshikawa, Koji Ikeda, Mikiko Uemura, Noriaki Maeshige
pmc-13205805.description: Highlights What are the main findings? A model-based cost–consequence analysis translating 14-day randomized crossover trial data estimated that electrical stimulation (ES) accelerated short-term pressure injury healing (Δ = 0.128 cm2/day; p = 0.008).Using DESIGN-R– and depth-stratified median time-to-heal imputation, ES was estimated to reduce time to heal by 126.

pmc-13409340.title: Analysis of Diagnosis and Treatment of Active Lupus Enteritis Accompanied by Intestinal Pseudo‐Obstruction as the Initial Manifestation: A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-13409340.creator: Wenhan Zhuang, Meijun Ji, Pengfei Xu, Lijuan Wang, Jiyong Jing, Wensheng Pan, Chenjing Zhang, Yoshifumi Nakayama

pmc-13639583.title: Targeting Exportin-1 in Cancer: From Nuclear Export to Oncogenic Transcriptional Hubs
pmc-13639583.creator: Seigi Oshima, Kensuke Kanaoka, Wataru Saika, Daichi Inoue
pmc-13639583.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Maintaining cellular homeostasis requires precise coordination of molecular trafficking between the nucleus and the cytoplasm. Central to this process is the nucleocytoplasmic transport system, which governs the spatial distribution of proteins and RNA. Exportin-1 (XPO1), also known as chromosome region maintenance 1 (CRM1), is the principal nuclear export receptor responsible for the transport of hundreds of cargo proteins bearing leucine-rich nuclear export signals. In a wide range of malignancies, XPO1 is frequently dysregulated through overexpression or recurrent somatic mutations.
